stem: Most car air bags contain a capsule of sodium azide, $\text{NaN}_3$. In a crash, the $\text{NaN}_3$ decomposes into its elements.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Write an equation for the decomposition of $\text{NaN}_3$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Complete the dot-and-cross diagram for the azide ion, $\text{N}_3^-$.

Use the following key for the electrons:

- ● electrons from central nitrogen atom
- × electrons from the other two nitrogen atoms
- □ added electron(s) responsible for the overall negative charge

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Lattice energies are always negative showing that they represent exothermic changes.
parts.text: Explain what is meant by the term lattice energy.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why lattice energy represents an exothermic change.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
Use the following data and any relevant data from the Data Booklet to calculate the standard enthalpy change of formation, $\Delta H_\text{f}^{\ominus}$, of $\text{NaN}_3\text{(s)}$.

Include a sign in your answer. Show all your working.

|  |  |
| :--- | :--- |
| lattice energy, $\Delta H_{\text{latt}}^{\ominus}$, of $\text{NaN}_3\text{(s)}$ | $-732\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| standard enthalpy change of atomisation, $\Delta H_{\text{at}}^{\ominus}$, of $\text{Na(g)}$ | $+107\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ |
| standard enthalpy change, $\Delta H^{\ominus}$, for $1\frac{1}{2}\text{N}_2(\text{g}) + \text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{N}_3^-(\text{g})$ | $+142\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ |

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.stem: The lattice energy, $\Delta H_{\text{latt}}^{\ominus}$, of $\text{RbN}_3\text{(s)}$ is $-636\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
parts.text: Suggest why the lattice energy of $\text{NaN}_3\text{(s)}$, $-732\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, is more exothermic than that of $\text{RbN}_3\text{(s)}$.
